author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected afterwards. Its correction shows the current date and description, applies the same rules as booking, updates that visit rather than adding a second, and returns to the owner's record. Cancelling stays out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the same form used for booking is shown, carrying that visit's current date and description.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries them and the owner's record is shown.
Given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet holds the same number of visits as before.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then the change is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then the change is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, still declined)
Any link or button reaching the correction from the owner's record or any other page
Correcting anything about a visit beyond its date and its description
notes: PRD id: this slice lands as REQ-VIS-003 in docs/prd.md, under the Visits capability area; the log's req_id stays REQ-VISITEDIT-001 for routing. NG-5 narrowed via docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md; the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR's status now points at it. The ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md still needs a row for the new ADR — that file is design-owned, not product-owned. The intake-decision record (handoff line 1) also states an address, a template, and a model attribute the owner named; those are owner-stated mechanism for the design stage to read there, not requirements. Three questions were left open rather than answered here, recorded in the PRD's Open Questions: a visible entry point (owner deferred it to a possible follow-up request), whether the future-date rule should hold for a visit whose date has passed (taken as yes, the narrowest reading), and whether a mismatched owner, pet, and visit should be refused (unspecified; booking refuses the equivalent).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction is the existing create-plus-edit controller pattern applied to visits. PetController already runs both flows from one controller, one shared createOrUpdatePetForm template, and a @ModelAttribute factory that branches on an optional path variable (findPet, PetController.java:75). VisitController gains the same shape: a /visits/{visitId}/edit GET and POST beside the existing /visits/new pair, the same pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm view, and the same `visit` model attribute the owner named at intake (handoff line 1). No new package, no new layer, no new dependency; system-design.md's feature-package structure and Owner-as-aggregate-entry invariant both hold unchanged. The one adjustment is inside loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:63): it is controller-wide, so it runs before the correction handlers too, and it currently always constructs a fresh Visit and attaches it with pet.addVisit(visit). It must branch on @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId — absent keeps today's booking behavior verbatim, present resolves the visit already held by the pet and attaches nothing. Attaching on the correction path is precisely what would give the pet a second visit record when the aggregate is saved.
integration_points: VisitController gains GET and POST for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, rendering the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm view
loadPetWithVisit becomes the single resolver for both flows, keyed on the optional visitId path variable

Resolve the visit by identity through the aggregate: add Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id) (Owner.java:117), keeping traversal inside the aggregate rather than filtering the collection in the controller

Update in place: form binding writes onto the resolved Visit, which is already a member of pet.getVisits(), so this.owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE through the existing Pet.visits CascadeType.ALL mapping — no second row, and no new repository
Redirect and flash follow processNewVisitForm: redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with a RedirectAttributes flash message
The non-future-date check and @Valid @NotBlank description carry over unchanged from processNewVisitForm (VisitController.java:100)

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute factory branching on @PathVariable(required = false) to serve create and edit from one controller — the precedent loadPetWithVisit should follow
getPet(Integer id): aggregate traversal by identity lives on the entity; Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors it
initUpdateForm / processUpdateForm route pair reusing the create-or-update template
Owner is the aggregate entry point and OwnerRepository the sole write path for the owner-pet-visit graph; the correction adds no repository

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit attaching a transient Visit on the correction path would persist an extra visit on save, breaking the unchanged-visit-count criterion
risks.mitigation: Attach only when visitId is absent; the correction path returns the visit already held by the pet

risks.risk: visitId is attacker-controlled external input, and a mismatched owner, pet, and visit triple could otherwise reach another owner's visit
risks.mitigation: Resolve owner -> pet -> visit through the aggregate so a mismatch cannot resolve, and refuse it the way the missing-pet case already does (IllegalArgumentException naming identifiers only). This is the security-principles Realization row 'trusting cross-request state': each request re-resolves what it acts on. The error page renders exception text (system-design.md Known Defects), so the message carries identifiers and no internal detail

risks.risk: Identifier tampering through form binding on the new POST
risks.mitigation: The existing controller-wide @InitBinder disallows id and *.id (VisitController.java:51) and applies to the new mapping; visit identity comes from the path only. Covers the mass-assignment row of security-principles Realization

risks.risk: A new user-facing label would have to land in all eleven message bundles or fail I18nPropertiesSyncTest (REQ-LANG-002)
risks.mitigation: Introduce no new message key. The template already conditions its heading on visit['new'] and the form posts to the current URL with no th:action, so the correction renders correctly with no template change at all

risks.risk: In-place mutation of a Visit held in Pet.visits, a LinkedHashSet
risks.mitigation: Neither Visit nor BaseEntity overrides equals or hashCode, so set membership is identity-based and mutation is safe. A refused correction persists nothing: the handler returns before save and spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled

notes: No ADR is warranted: the product decision is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md (product-owned), and the how is an application of the recorded feature-package and Thymeleaf decisions with no hard-to-reverse trade-off. Durable-memory write made this dispatch: docs/adr/README.md gained the index row for the 2026-08-15 non-goal ADR, and the 2026-08-08 row's status now records the NG-5 narrowing. Deferred to doc-sync after the code lands, deliberately, because system-design.md's provenance banner states every statement describes what the code demonstrably does: the Contracts table rows for VisitController (purpose becomes booking and correction), Visit, Pet, Owner, and OwnerRepository each gain REQ-VIS-003 in the Implements column. Open questions recorded rather than answered, per the intake: (1) the correction form's submit button reads 'Add Visit' (#{addVisit}) and its heading loses the 'New' prefix — no requirement names either, so the narrow reading changes neither and adds no bundle key; (2) the PRD's own three open questions stand — a visible entry point, the future-date rule for an already-passed visit, and refusal of a mismatched triple. This design answers (2)'s third question structurally by resolving through the aggregate, but whether the reader should see the error page or a not-found remains a product question; matching the existing missing-pet behavior is the narrow reading taken here. Template listed as supporting, not primary: the prd-entry names it a file target, but the acceptance criteria are met without touching it. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is skipped.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain was NOT verified against the NVD in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access. The diff changes no dependency declaration, so the resolved set is unchanged from the reviewed baseline (Spring Boot 4.1.0), but treat the CVE check as not run rather than clean - a human or CI should close it.

Not a finding under docs/security-principles.md (it is the recorded baseline, unchanged by this diff): processUpdateVisitForm binds @ModelAttribute Owner and saves it, so owner fields submitted alongside the visit form are persisted without @Valid - identical to the pre-existing processNewVisitForm. Worth carrying into any future decision about over-posting on the Owner model attribute, but it is not made worse here.

The visit-correction POST is a new state-changing endpoint with no CSRF token, matching the application-wide baseline of no CSRF protection. Recorded so that if CSRF is ever added, this route is on the list.
approved_aspects: Trusting cross-request state: loadPetWithVisit re-resolves owner -> pet -> visit from the repository on every request, and processUpdateVisitForm re-applies the future-date rule via the shared rejectNonFutureDate. No handler trusts an identifier because an earlier request validated it.

Insecure direct object reference: the visit is resolved only through pet.getVisit(visitId) on a pet resolved only through owner.getPet(petId), so a visitId belonging to another pet or owner yields null and is refused. Pet.getVisit additionally skips unsaved visits, so a transient visit cannot be addressed by id.

Mass assignment: VisitController's existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") covers both new endpoints; neither adds a binder that omits the disallow list, and no request-bound identifier reaches the entity.

Cross-site scripting: the reused pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template renders visit date and description through th:text only. No th:utext, no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__), no request-derived value in an href or inline script.

Exposed surface: the change adds two routes (GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit) and states them in the PRD and the ADR. Both are no more open than the existing visit-booking POST; actuator exposure is untouched.

Error output: the new IllegalArgumentException message interpolates only path-bound Integers (visitId, petId), so no credential, connection string, or session identifier reaches the rendered error page. Non-numeric input fails type conversion before the message is built.
Data access: no new query text. Persistence goes through OwnerRepository.save on a managed aggregate, so no string-concatenated SQL is introduced.
Concurrency: the controller stays stateless (only the injected repository as a field); Pet.getVisit adds no shared mutable state to the singleton bean.
No deserialization, file, path, process, network, or randomness surface is introduced; no secret-shaped literal appears anywhere in the diff.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Jacoco confirms the mismatched/missing-visitId path is completely untested: Pet.getVisit has 2 missed branches (the not-found -> return null path) and VisitController.loadPetWithVisit has 2 missed branches (the visit==null -> throw new IllegalArgumentException path), both 0% covered. This is exactly the risk the superseding design-block (handoff line 10) names under 'risks': 'visitId is attacker-controlled external input, and a mismatched owner, pet, and visit triple could otherwise reach another owner's visit,' mitigated by resolving through the aggregate and refusing with an IllegalArgumentException. The mitigation exists in code but is unverified by any test — the same gap exists for both the GET /edit and POST /edit routes.
findings.fix: Add a test (e.g. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitDoesNotBelongToThePet) that requests GET (and/or POST) /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit with a visitId the pet does not hold, and asserts the IllegalArgumentException path is exercised (e.g. via MockMvc's resolved exception, matching the existing missing-owner/missing-pet precedent style if one exists, or asserting a 5xx/exception outcome).

findings.description: docs/prd.md Visits edge case 3 (added by this slice) reads: 'A visit whose date has passed can be corrected only by moving that date into the future, because the booking rule applies unchanged.' No test exercises a booked visit whose original date has already passed. BOOKED_VISIT_DATE is fixed at now+7 (always future) across every test in this class, so the scenario the edge case describes — correcting an already-past-dated visit — is never set up. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheDateIsNotInTheFuture only submits today's date against the existing future-dated booked visit; it does not construct a visit that is itself already in the past.
findings.fix: Add a dedicated test (e.g. via a bookedVisit(LocalDate) overload or a second factory) that books a visit with a past date, opens/submits its correction, and asserts the future-date rule still applies (refused when the submitted date is not in the future, accepted when moved into the future) — matching prd.md's edge case 3 numbering.

approved_aspects: Test names follow the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school and match the prd-entry's test_names exactly
Data values use named Tier-1/Tier-2 constants (BOOKED_VISIT_ID, CORRECTED_VISIT_DATE, etc.) with no bare mystery literals
New construction is wrapped in a bookedVisit() factory rather than calling the Visit constructor inline in each test
AssertJ used for the new state assertions (assertThat(...).isEqualTo/hasSize); MockMvc/hamcrest matchers for model attributes match the file's existing idiom
All five prd-entry acceptance criteria (form prefill, update-in-place, unchanged visit count, blank-description refusal, non-future-date refusal) have a dedicated passing test
Mocking stays within policy: MockitoBean only on OwnerRepository (the sanctioned Spring web-layer boundary), no mocking of Pet/Visit/Owner value objects

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: One module and one feature package: VisitController plus a Pet.getVisit lookup, 82 production lines across 2 files, no sensitive paths, no dependency or configuration change; the rest is PRD and ADR prose. The existing booking flow is touched only where loadPetWithVisit gains an optional visitId, and its no-visitId branch is the old body verbatim.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: the correction branch returns the visit the pet already holds without re-attaching it, which is exactly what keeps the visit count flat; the extracted rejectNonFutureDate carries the date boundary over unchanged, with no flip; the visit is resolved through the owner-pet aggregate so a foreign visitId cannot be reached; Visit has no equals or hashCode override, so mutating a member of Pet's LinkedHashSet is safe. The one thing to know rather than a surprise: a mismatched visitId throws IllegalArgumentException and surfaces as a 500 rather than a 404, matching the controller's existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found precedent, and the tests codify that.

test_adequacy.note: Nine new tests assert real outcomes, not the implementation: they read the corrected visit back off the pet and check its date and description, assert the visit count is unchanged (the bug the design feared), check both validation refusals by field and error code, exercise the past-dated visit in both directions, and drive the foreign-visitId path on GET and POST. They would fail against a re-attaching or non-mutating implementation. Two round-1 test gaps were named by the test reviewer and closed in round 2.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved with empty findings in round 2, but the security reviewer parked three recommendations on that approval, one of which asks for a human: the supply chain was not verified against the NVD (no dependency-check plugin, no network), so the CVE check is not run rather than clean. It also carries forward, as unchanged baseline, that processUpdateVisitForm binds and saves the Owner model attribute without validation and that the new state-changing POST carries no CSRF token; both mirror processNewVisitForm, so the change adds a second endpoint with the same pre-existing exposure rather than worsening it.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the intake decision line for line: the NG-5 narrowing and its ADR, the two URL-only routes, no owner-detail link, and the deferred entry point recorded as an open question rather than built. The single design revision was bookkeeping, not a scope fight: the superseding design-block only took ownership of two ADR paths the first one left uncovered for the autofix audit. Zero build retries after it, zero consultations.

rationale: Correct and tightly scoped: the correction updates in place, the aggregate lookup blocks a foreign visitId, and the tests prove both. Read the security reviewer's parked recommendations before merging - the CVE check was not run, and the new POST inherits the app-wide missing CSRF and Owner over-posting baseline.
